A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MemOCR work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison; retained material can be matched despite pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original QA experiments, training-objective ablations, layout analyses, runtime measurements, and failure cases.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, conversational-memory evaluation, transfer and robustness tests, and training analyses.

M1.justification: The rich-text drafting, image rendering, visual reading, three training objectives, and GRPO advantage aggregation remain unchanged. Alternative readers and training datasets are experimental variants, not revisions to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v5 adds LOCOMO conversational-memory evaluation and MMLU general-knowledge testing, substantially extending coverage beyond the original four document-QA benchmarks. Appendix D.7 also uses NQ for alternative RL training, whereas v4 used it only for evaluation.

E2.justification: New Table 2 evaluates SimpleMem, LightMem, and HyMem against MemOCR; these were absent from v4's evaluated comparator set. Table 3b adds a MemAgent variant using summarization instead of truncation. Existing baselines remain, and the renamed 72B ablation is the same comparator.

E3.justification: v5 adds comparisons granting text baselines four times the token budget, summarization-based budget control, GPT-4o reading, rendering-shape controls, and 1,000-step training-data and convergence comparisons. C.2 also revises the reported GPU allocation and training duration without establishing reruns. The original QA evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v4's layout, objective, scaling, and failure analyses, v5 tests budget and truncation confounds and adds reader transfer, aspect-ratio robustness, MMLU capability retention, training-data ablation, and convergence analysis in D.4–D.8. These address several previously untested explanations and applicability boundaries.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-run means, appendix standard deviations and independent two-sample t-tests, and five renderer runs. The added tables introduce no new uncertainty estimates, seed-count disclosures, or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation, statistical, runtime, and scaling results are retained. New outcomes include 58.5% for MemAgent with summarization versus 62.2% for MemOCR at 16 tokens and 10K context, LOCOMO scores of 33.14% versus Mem-α's 23.83% at 1024 tokens, and MMLU scores of 71.1% versus the base model's 72.5%. Transfer, rendering, training-data, and convergence results are also added.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, memory-cost argument, optimization equations, and Appendix D.2 complexity assumptions and derivations remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction appears.

C1.justification: The headline method and efficiency claims remain. The introduction newly distinguishes MemOCR from prior visual compressors through learned content selection and spatial allocation, providing a limited refinement of the novelty claim.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive interpretations concerning baseline fairness, conversational and reader transfer, typography rather than absolute coordinates, limited general-capability loss, multi-hop training transfer, and convergence behavior. The original limitations and failure explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: C.2 changes the reported training resources from 64 H800 GPUs for 14 days to 32 for 7 days, while retaining approximately 21,000 GPU-hours per model. That retained total is inconsistent with the revised allocation. Existing pipeline instructions, prompts, hyperparameters, and code-access information otherwise remain stable.

R1.justification: v5 adds references for SimpleMem, HyMem, and LOCOMO and an introductory contrast with prior visual-compression methods. Appendix A remains unchanged. The revised title of the Du et al. reference identifies the same cited work.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to an introductory positioning paragraph, additional Section 4.2 observations, and new D.4–D.8 subsections. Most existing prose and section order remain intact. The publication footer, 72B comparator label, and hyperparameter-table heading also receive small edits.

P2.justification: v5 substantially expands the empirical displays with a RAG comparison table, a three-panel fairness/generalization table, and five appendix analysis tables. Table 3a rearranges existing scores across budgets. The original eight figures and existing tables are retained, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens the empirical case by addressing v4's reliance on hard-truncated textual baselines. Table 3b shows that summarization raises MemAgent from 31.6% to 58.5% at 16 tokens, narrowing its gap to MemOCR's 62.2% and making the comparison more informative. Budget, transfer, and robustness controls further strengthen validity. Sparse implementation details for new experiments and the introduced GPU-hour inconsistency limit reproducibility, but the overall gain in evidential quality is substantial.
